"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-arithmetic-sequence-after-changing-at-most-one-element/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

3872. Longest Arithmetic Sequence After Changing At Most One Element

You are given an integer array nums.

A subarray is arithmetic if the difference between consecutive elements in the subarray is constant.

You can replace at most one element in nums with any integer. Then, you select an arithmetic subarray from nums.

Return an integer denoting the maximum length of the arithmetic subarray you can select.

Example 1:

Input: nums = [9,7,5,10,1]
Output: 5
Explanation:
Replace nums[3] = 10 with 3. The array becomes [9, 7, 5, 3, 1].
Select the subarray [9, 7, 5, 3, 1], which is arithmetic because consecutive elements have a common difference of -2.

Example 2:

Input: nums = [1,2,6,7]
Output: 3
Explanation:
Replace nums[0] = 1 with -2. The array becomes [-2, 2, 6, 7].
Select the subarray [-2, 2, 6], 7, which is arithmetic because consecutive elements have a common difference of 4.

Constraints:

    4 <= nums.length <= 10^5
    1 <= nums[i] <= 10^5
"""


class Solution:
    def longestArithmetic(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        if n <= 2:
            return n
        # left[i]: length of longest arithmetic subarray ending at i
        left = [0] * n
        left[0] = 1
        left[1] = 2
        for i in range(2, n):
            if nums[i] - nums[i - 1] == nums[i - 1] - nums[i - 2]:
                left[i] = left[i - 1] + 1
            else:
                left[i] = 2
        # right[i]: length of longest arithmetic subarray starting at i
        right = [0] * n
        right[n - 1] = 1
        right[n - 2] = 2
        for i in range(n - 3, -1, -1):
            if nums[i + 1] - nums[i] == nums[i + 2] - nums[i + 1]:
                right[i] = right[i + 1] + 1
            else:
                right[i] = 2
        ans = max(left)  # best without any change
        # consider changing each position
        for i in range(n):
            if i == 0:
                # change first element to extend right side
                ans = max(ans, 1 + (right[1] if n > 1 else 0))
            elif i == n - 1:
                # change last element to extend left side
                ans = max(ans, 1 + (left[n - 2] if n > 1 else 0))
            else:
                # try to merge left ending at i-1 and right starting at i+1 by changing nums[i]
                # if nums[i+1] - nums[i-1] is even, we can set nums[i] to make a common integer diff
                if (nums[i + 1] - nums[i - 1]) % 2 == 0:
                    merged = left[i - 1] + 1 + right[i + 1]
                    ans = max(ans, merged)
                # even if can't perfectly merge, we can at least extend one side by changing nums[i]
                ans = max(ans, left[i - 1] + 1, right[i + 1] + 1)
        if ans > n:
            ans = n
        return ans


sol = Solution()

print(sol.longestArithmetic([9, 7, 5, 10, 1]))  # 5

assert sol.longestArithmetic([9, 7, 5, 10, 1]) == 5
assert sol.longestArithmetic([1, 2, 6, 7]) == 3

assert sol.longestArithmetic([1, 3, 5, 7]) == 4
assert sol.longestArithmetic([5, 5, 5, 5, 5]) == 5
assert sol.longestArithmetic([-1, -3, -5, -7]) == 4
assert sol.longestArithmetic(list(range(100000))) == 100000
assert sol.longestArithmetic([7] * 100000) == 100000
assert sol.longestArithmetic([1, 3, 5, 100, 9, 11, 13]) == 7
assert sol.longestArithmetic([1, 2, 10, 5]) == 3
assert sol.longestArithmetic([42]) == 1
assert sol.longestArithmetic([1, 2]) == 2
assert sol.longestArithmetic([1, 2, 3]) == 3
